FOR campaign/hornvale-observation-series -- HELD AT `outboard`, NOT `gate`, AND YOUR LOGIC IS ACTUALLY CORRECT. 4dbef7a0e51b. This is a lint, and a small one.

  artifacts  309.4s  rc=0
  outboard    98.3s  rc=1   <- shellcheck

  In scripts/observation-film.sh line 59:
  [ "$out_leaf" != "." ] && [ "$out_leaf" != ".." ] || die "refusing broad output target: $out"
                         ^-- SC2015 (info): A && B || C is not if-then-else.

FIRST, SO YOU DO NOT GO HUNTING FOR A BUG: trace it and the guard is right.

  leaf is "."   -> A false          -> die     correct
  leaf is ".."  -> A true, B false  -> die     correct
  anything else -> A true, B true   -> no die  correct

SC2015 warns about the general footgun in `A && B || C` -- C can fire when A
succeeded but B failed, which people usually do not intend. Here that is
exactly what you DO intend, so the code does what you meant. shellcheck cannot
tell those apart, and this repo's Makefile treats even info-level findings as
failures, so it stops the phase regardless.

THE FIX I WOULD MAKE, because it is clearer than a disable directive:

  case "$out_leaf" in
    .|..) die "refusing broad output target: $out" ;;
  esac

Same behaviour, no lint, and it reads as what it is -- a refusal list -- rather
than a boolean chain a reader has to trace. A `# shellcheck disable=SC2015`
with a justification comment would also pass, but the case form removes the
question instead of answering it.

WORTH KNOWING FOR NEXT TIME: `make quick` runs fmt, clippy and type-audit but
NOT shellcheck; the shellcheck target is part of `outboard`, which only runs in
the chamber. So a new shell script's first contact with shellcheck is a queue
row. You can get ahead of it locally:

  shellcheck scripts/observation-film.sh

CLAUDE.md asks for exactly that on any shell script before committing, and it
costs a second. Nothing else in your submission was reached -- gate and clients
never ran -- so there may or may not be more behind this; the next run will
tell you.
